solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ace stuff in broadcast round US capital

indicators.note: one thing placed in another means the earlier pieces sit inside the word that follows

parts.note: a signal broadcast is sent out
O is round in shape
A is the card abbreviation for an ace
to stuff is to cram

explanation.surface: A tennis player's ace, padded into a televised round, in an American capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ace' tempts as a tennis term, but it is the card abbreviation; Sacramento is a state capital, not the national one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacramento is the state capital of California, so it is a capital city in the United States.

clue.text: Small firm finally went national

parts.note: S is the clothing abbreviation for small
Co. abbreviates company, a firm

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the following word, its closing letter

parts.note: the closing letter of this word

explanation.surface: A small business at last became nationalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' is a noun here: a citizen of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scot is a person from Scotland, and a national is a citizen of a particular nation.

clue.text: Bread and serving of butter included in tea

indicators.note: something included in another is placed within it

parts.note: chai is tea, especially spiced Indian tea
a pat is a small portion of butter

explanation.surface: Bread with a portion of butter, served at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: Chai, now common in English, is the Hindi word for tea, fitting the Indian bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is an unleavened flatbread from South Asian cooking, a kind of bread.

clue.text: Dispute resulting from deviously tough teasers

indicators.note: something done deviously takes a winding, crooked route, so these letters are twisted around

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An argument provoked by fiendishly hard puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teasers' suggests crossword clues, apt for a puzzle about puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue the toss is a British idiom for disputing a decision already made, so it means to dispute.

clue.text: Was a trainee being denied an opening merited?

indicators.note: denied an opening means losing its first letter, the start of the word

parts.note: a trainee learned the job

explanation.surface: Asking whether an apprentice who missed out on a job deserved it.
explanation.walkthrough: LEARNED drops its L.
explanation.definitionFit: If something is earned it is deserved through effort, so earned matches merited as a past-tense verb.

clue.text: Simple shirt, a "large", to keep young child dry

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the earlier pieces hold the next one within

parts.note: a tee is a plain T-shirt
a tot is a small child
taken as written
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A plain large T-shirt to keep a toddler from getting wet.
explanation.walkthrough: TEE and A L together hold TOT: TEE + TOT + AL. 'Dry' looks like the opposite of wet; it means not drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry person or place forbids alcohol, so dry is a synonym of abstaining or teetotal.

clue.text: Despicable people run away from mêlée

indicators.note: something taken away from a word is removed from it, leaving the rest

parts.note: a scrum is a confused, jostling crowd
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Nasty types flee a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: SCRUM loses its R to leave SCUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Scum is a contemptuous term for the lowest, most worthless people in society.

clue.text: Supplier of food and drink mostly consumed by home worker

indicators.note: something consumed is swallowed, ending up inside the eater

parts.note: a home carer looks after people in their homes

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A provider of meals and beverages, most of them eaten by someone working at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food and drink' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at food; drink belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer provides meals for events and functions, so is a supplier of food.

clue.text: Bloke bound to hide one principal motive

indicators.note: to hide something is to conceal it, keeping it inside

parts.note: a bloke is a man
I is the Roman numeral one
to bound is to leap or spring

explanation.surface: A man obliged to conceal one central reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' reads as obliged, but here it is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainspring is the chief spring in a clock, and figuratively the chief driving force behind something.

clue.text: Park official that is overwhelmed by huge greenhouses?

indicators.note: being overwhelmed means being surrounded and swallowed up by something else

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a park ranger patrols a national park
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A park warden is dwarfed by enormous glasshouses.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that an orangery is only one kind of greenhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: An orangery is a glazed building for growing citrus trees, a type of greenhouse.

clue.text: A case of hefty unit oddly not used

indicators.note: if the odd-placed letters are not used, only the even-placed ones remain

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of these two words

explanation.surface: An example of a heavy item left unused.
explanation.walkthrough: A crossword favourite: an etui is a small ornamental case for needles or cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small decorative container for sewing needles or toiletries, so it is a kind of case.

clue.text: Research flop possibly leading to blame being placed internally

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements of these letters

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A failed study prompting someone to blame those within the organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Placed internally' sounds like an inside culprit, but it means blame aimed inwards at oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-reproach is blaming oneself, so the blame is directed inward rather than at others.

clue.text: Cook adores pig feet — a delicacy

indicators.note: to cook is to doctor or falsify, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to cook trotters, which someone loves, as a gourmet treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a kitchen instruction for the trotters, which suits the surface, but it only signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Pâté de foie gras, made from fattened goose or duck liver, is a famous French luxury food.

clue.text: Like individuals absorbing current criticisms

parts.note: as and like both mean in the manner of

indicators.note: absorbing means soaking something up and taking it in

parts.note: individuals are persons
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: As though people were taking in up-to-date complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as up-to-date, but it is electrical current, symbol I.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspersions are damaging remarks, as in casting aspersions, so they are attacks or criticisms.

clue.text: Singular, amusing insult

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
light entertainment is amusing rather than serious

explanation.surface: An odd, funny put-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' reads as 'remarkable' in the surface, but it is just its grammatical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight is a snub or affront, an act of disrespect, so it works as a noun for an insult.

clue.text: Traveller much less biased, we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: way means by far, and fairer means less biased

explanation.surface: Someone on the road who is far more impartial, or so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way' is informal for 'much', as in way better.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer is someone journeying on foot, an old word for a traveller.

clue.text: Righteous type rather short with celebs

indicators.note: something short is cut down, missing its final letter

parts.note: rather and more both express preference or degree
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A virtuous person who is somewhat brief with famous people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rather short' reads as somewhat curt, but short applies to the word for rather.
explanation.definitionFit: A moralist preaches about right and wrong, a self-consciously virtuous person.

clue.text: Choice of putting up with Liberal instead of Republican

indicators.note: one thing used instead of another takes its place in the word

parts.note: putting up a building is its erection
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A political choice: tolerating a Liberal rather than a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: The R of ERECTION is swapped for an L. 'Putting up with' sounds like tolerating, but 'putting up' is the construction sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An election is a vote, the act of choosing someone for office.

clue.text: Agreement made by two hospital departments ending in failure

parts.note: ENT, the ear, nose and throat department, twice

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of this word

explanation.surface: A pact between two hospital units that comes to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department, a common hospital ward abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale, an agreement.

clue.text: Precise study involving trouble

indicators.note: something involving another takes it in, holding it within itself

parts.note: a den is a private study room
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Careful research that lands someone in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study' reads as research, but it is a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead on is an idiom for exactly right or accurate, so it can stand for precise.

clue.text: Sea animal toy — one from Lapland, say

indicators.note: say means the words are spoken, so their sound gives the answer

parts.note: a doll is a toy, and a Finn comes from Finland, which includes much of Lapland

explanation.surface: A toy sea creature, maybe a reindeer-land souvenir.
explanation.walkthrough: Lapland spans northern Norway, Sweden and Finland, so a Laplander may be a Finn.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolphin is a marine mammal, a creature of the sea.

clue.text: Salt Lake City resident I see now in Austin regularly

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
regularly means at even intervals, taking every other letter

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
aha is the cry of sudden understanding

explanation.surface: A Utah city dweller finally understands, while in Texas.
explanation.walkthrough: Austin is the capital of Texas, a red herring beside Salt Lake City.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt Lake City is the capital of Utah, so someone living there is a Utahan.

clue.text: Solitary facts I dealt with well

indicators.note: cards that are dealt with are shuffled and redistributed, so these letters get a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Isolated facts handled competently by the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' at the end looks like a casual remark but it is the definition, an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something satisfactorily means doing it adequately or properly, an adverbial synonym of well.

clue.text: You're right in the first instance to have regrets

indicators.note: the first instance of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of this word
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Admitting someone was right from the start, and being sorry about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: 'True!' is what you say to agree.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'True' concedes a point, the same as telling someone they are correct.

clue.text: Has American sprinter to lack energy?

indicators.note: to lack something is to be without it, so it is dropped from the name

parts.note: Jesse Owens, the US athlete who won four golds at the 1936 Olympics
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an American runner has run out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: OWENS loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to possess it, so owns is a present-tense synonym of has.

clue.text: Attractive guy perhaps had been a lady's kitchen helper

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
was and had been are both past forms of be
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A handsome man who used to be some woman's help around the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks a guy as only one example of a dish, which can be any good-looking person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishwasher, person or machine, helps in the kitchen by cleaning the plates.

clue.text: Discard fresh, edible sandwiches

indicators.note: a sandwich holds a filling between its slices, so the letters sit inside these words

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Throw away good fresh sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like the noun being thrown away, but it is a verb holding the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed something is to cast it off or get rid of it, as a tree drops leaves.

clue.text: Group of rocks, in a single layer, gets moved outside

indicators.note: a word placed outside another wraps around it, enclosing it
something moved is shifted out of place, so these letters change order

parts.note: a hen is a bird that lays eggs
the letters to be rearranged
a single thing is one

explanation.surface: A set of stones arranged in one stratum that shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'layer' is not a stratum of rock, as the surface suggests, but a laying hen.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonehenge is the prehistoric circle of standing stones on Salisbury Plain in England.
